newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 19.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In recent weeks China has postponed ministerial visits to and from Australia without explanation and the Chinese Government has declined to act on a request from the Australian Government to correct a stream of attacks on Australian policy in the official Chinese press - two strong indications of the strain between the two countries. Page 1.

Telstra is considering franchising key areas of its customer premises equipment (CPE) business, in a bid to stem annual losses of A$200 million. The move, which chief executive Frank Blount says will boost productivity, has received strong opposition from the Communications Electrical and Plumbers Union, who say they are prepared to fight the issue through the industrial relations court. Page 3.

A report released by the Australian National Audit Office has suggested a way in which the Australian Taxation Office could add more than A$142 million a year to Commonwealth revenue. The report found that revenue could increase through the introduction of more timely payments by taxpayers and improvements in the effectiveness of debt recovery. Page 3.

New codes introduced by the Federal Government regarding telecommunications cabling could impose a A$10 million fine to either Optus or Telstra if they breached the new regulations. The code requires the telecommunications giants to place all cabling at major intersections underground. Communications Minister Richard Alston has also recommended regulator Austel be given more power to check on the carrier's rollout. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to a preliminary assessment for the Howard Government, a stricken seven-tonne Russian Mars probe carrying plutonium orbited out of control and passed over the east coast of Australia, south of Sydney, just fifteen minutes before it crashed into he Pacific Ocean. A more detailed report on the path of the space craft is expected to be handed to the Government soon. Page 1.

Speaking at the 1996 Sir Robert Menzies Lecture in Melbourne last night, Prime Minister John Howard sought to recast his image by redefining the boundaries of the Liberal Party to include the "new constituency" of battlers and families struggling to get ahead, which helped him win the March 2 election. Page 1.

Qantas Airways has attributed a 2.5 percent rise in domestic airfares from tomorrow to rising jet fuel prices and says it is also considering a similar increase for some of its international airfares. Ansett is likely to follow the move later this week as the two airlines have traditionally matched each other's domestic fares structure. Page 1.

A coronial inquest into the drug-related deaths of two friends, Christopher Rex Dingo and Stephen Mallison, began in Darwin yesterday and the hearing heard that the doctor who helped the first man to die under the world's only voluntary euthanasia law, Phlip Nitschke, prescribed methadone to the two men shortly before they died. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Calming serious bilateral tensions will be Prime Minister John Howard's main focus for this weekend's meeting with Chinese President Jiang Zemin. The meeting will be the highlight of talks taking place between world leaders at next Sunday's Asia Pacific Eonomic Co-operation (APEC) summit. Page 1.

A report by the New South Wales Child Protection Council has revealed there is a growing incidence in the State of children being abused by other children. The report said early detection and treatment of children who exhibited this sort of behaviour was in dire need and recommended changes to the management of child, juvenile and adult sex offenders. Page 1.

Restrictions on junior doctor providers numbers have sparked a new wave of action among senior GPs and specialists, with the possibility of a national day of action involving doctors, GPs and hospitals. Doctors meeting in Canberra gave the Australian Medical Association executive the green light to take any action it feels necessary to force the Government to back down. Page 3.

A new drug which has significantly enhanced performance on simple memory tests is to be tested on patients suffering from Alzheimer's disease. United States researchers have reported the results of the first human trials and revealed it had no side-effect and the improvement appeared to be greatest among elderly people. Page 3.
THE AGE

Emergency services in several States were on full alert for more than three hours yesterday following a warning from US President Bill Clinton to Prime Minister John Howard that a plummeting Russian Mars probe was likely to land in Australia - the space probe eventually landed in the Pacific Ocean. Page A1.

Victorian Opposition health spokesman John Thwaites released figured obtained under freedom of information legislation yesterday indicating hospital waiting lists had blown out to more than 40,000, a 22 per cent increase from October 1 1992 - the month the Kennett Government came to power - including 11,335 "hidden" on booking lists. Page A1.

The resignation of a senior manager of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority has raised new doubts about the standard of Australia's air safety. Director of aviation medicine, Dr Robert Liddell, said decisions made by senior management at the authority had seriously undermined air safety. Page A1.

Chinese medicine practitioners will have to be registered if legislation on the matter is passed in the Victorian Parliament. Authors of a report into Chinese herbal medicine found evidence of deaths linked with the abuse of the medicine in three States oer the past eight years, and recommended that regulations be introduced to control the practice. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
